从树冠到草尖，走进植物共同构成的立体世界。: Explore the living space from crowns to grass tips.
比较森林、草地与湿地的外貌。: Compare the appearance of forests, grasslands and wetlands.
不只看一棵树，也看它的邻居。: Look at a plant and its neighbors.
地表之下，根系也在利用空间。: Roots also share and occupy space.
同一片景观中的植被，为什么不是整齐一致的？: Why is vegetation within one landscape so varied?
植被是一个地区植物群落的总体。局地水分、土壤、地形和干扰的差异，使不同植物在不同: Vegetation comprises a region's plant communities. Differences in moisture, soil, terrain and disturbance create interconnected local habitats.
先比较植物的高矮、疏密和叶片，再给森林、草地、湿地找到位置。: Compare height, density and leaves, then locate forest, grassland and wetland.
区分“植物个体”“植物群落”与“植被”，讨论局地生境的空间异质性。: Distinguish individual plants, communities and vegetation; discuss spatial habitat variation.
这是复合生境的教学拼景，不代表一个真实地点；树木、根系及土层比例经过可视化调整。: This teaching collage is not a real location. Tree, root and soil proportions are adjusted for visibility.
逐层观察乔木、灌木和草本，让被遮住的生命显现出来。: Reveal trees, shrubs and herbs layer by layer.
从外部观察树冠与高低差异。: Observe the crown shapes and height differences.
降低乔木层的不透明度，寻找灌木与草本。: Reduce tree opacity to reveal shrubs and herbs.
透视根系，联系枯落物与地表。: Reveal roots and relate litter to the soil surface.
森林中的植物，为什么会有高低不同的层次？: Why do forest plants occupy different heights?
不同植物的生活型、生长高度与耐阴能力不同。上层树冠截获较多光照，能适应较弱光照的: Plants differ in growth form, height and shade tolerance. Crowns intercept much of the light; shade-tolerant plants can live below. The resulting structure varies among forest types.
识别乔木、灌木与草本三个生活型，找出它们所在的大致高度。: Identify trees, shrubs and herbs and their approximate heights.
联系光照差异、生态位与空间利用；注意藤本和附生植物不一定只属于一个高度层。: Relate light, niches and use of space. Vines and epiphytes may span several height layers.
本章用三种生活型展示基本分层，不把它当作所有森林的固定层数；根系和土壤仅作辅助示: Three growth forms illustrate basic layering, not a fixed number of layers for every forest. Roots and soil are schematic.
切换六种典型植被，比较外貌，而不是只记住名字。: Compare six typical vegetation forms, beyond memorizing names.
比较植株的高矮、疏密与优势生活型。: Compare height, spacing and dominant growth forms.
找出这些形态可能解决的问题。: Ask what challenges these forms may help solve.
同一植被类型内部也存在差异。: Variation also occurs within each vegetation type.
荒漠里，植物是不是只有“把根扎得很深”一种办法？: Do all desert plants survive by growing very deep roots?
不是。不同荒漠植物可采用深根、广布浅根、缩小叶面积、储水或短暂生长等不同策略。图: No. Strategies include deep roots, broad shallow roots, small leaves, water storage and brief growth periods. The sparse shrubs shown here do not represent all desert roots.
把乔木占优势、草本占优势和植被稀疏三种外貌对应起来。: Compare tree-dominated, herb-dominated and sparse vegetation.
从形态特征提出适应假说，再讨论其他因素与反例；不把相关性当作单一因果。: Use form to propose adaptation hypotheses, then discuss other factors and counterexamples. Correlation is not a single cause.
六种场景展示典型外貌，未按照真实地点或统一比例重建；湿地可以分布在不同地带。: Six typical forms are illustrated without surveyed locations or a common scale. Wetlands occur in different climatic zones.
沿着观察线攀升，看看高大乔木如何让位于低矮植被。: Follow the observation line as tall trees give way to low vegetation.
追踪针叶林在坡面上的位置。: Locate conifer forest on the slope.
寻找低矮灌丛、草甸和稀疏植被。: Look for low shrubs, meadows and sparse vegetation.
所有山地都有这套植被带，林线也都在相同海拔吗？: Do all mountains share these belts and the same treeline elevation?
不是。山地植被带受纬度、山体高度、坡向、水热条件及干扰等影响。此处只展示一种简化: No. Latitude, mountain height, aspect, climate and disturbance affect zonation. This is one simplified combination, with no universal elevation boundaries.
自下而上描述植被外貌的变化，区分林线与山顶。: Describe changes upward and distinguish the treeline from the summit.
解释山麓基带、带谱完整程度和林线的地区差异，并讨论坡向影响。: Discuss regional differences in the base belt, available belts and treeline, including slope aspect.
观察高度是模型内的相对高度，不是实测海拔。本模型不代表某座山，也不是普适的植被带: The slider shows relative model height, not measured elevation. This is neither a specific mountain nor a universal sequence.
拖动季节轴，观察同一片落叶阔叶林的展叶、繁茂与落叶。: Scrub the season axis to watch one deciduous forest leaf out, fill in and shed leaves.
关注新叶展开与树冠变得浓密。: Watch leaves unfold and crowns become denser.
比较叶色和树冠覆盖的变化。: Compare leaf color and canopy cover.
枝干显露，枯落物回到地表。: Branches appear and litter returns to the ground.
冬季落叶，是树木死亡了吗？: Does winter leaf fall mean the trees have died?
不是。许多温带落叶树会在不利季节落叶并进入休眠，来年条件适宜时重新展叶。常绿与落: No. Many temperate deciduous trees shed leaves and become dormant during unfavorable seasons, then leaf out again. Evergreen trees also replace leaves; evergreen habit, leaf lifespan and shedding time are distinct concepts.
用“同一片森林”排除地点差异，描述叶色与疏密的季节变化。: Keeping the same forest removes location differences. Describe seasonal color and density changes.
比较常绿与落叶策略，指出具体物候时间因树种、纬度和年份而变化。: Compare evergreen and deciduous strategies. Phenology varies with species, latitude and year.
本章只模拟落叶阔叶林。季相节点与冬季积雪是示例，不对应某年的物候日历。: Only a deciduous broadleaf forest is modeled. Seasonal stages and winter snow are examples, not a dated phenological calendar.
从土壤仍保留的裸地出发，观察一种可能的植被恢复过程。: Explore one recovery pathway where soil remains after disturbance.
裸露地表之下，土壤仍然存在。: Soil remains beneath the bare surface.
草本、灌木和幼树逐渐改变优势。: Herbs, shrubs and young trees change in dominance.
森林只是适宜条件下的一种可能。: Forest is one possibility under suitable conditions.
是不是只要一直等待，任何草地最终都会变成森林？: Will every grassland eventually become a forest if we wait?
不是。此处假设环境适宜森林且没有持续的强干扰。水分、土壤、种源、火、放牧和人为活: No. This example assumes forest-suitable conditions without persistent strong disturbance. Moisture, soil, seed sources, fire, grazing and people can change the path. Succession is not a universal one-way staircase.
描述植被覆盖与高度的变化，知道这是一段过程而非几张地点照片。: Describe changing cover and height as a process, not photographs of different locations.
比较初生与次生演替的起点，讨论干扰、种源和多种恢复路径；不套用固定年数。: Compare primary and secondary starting conditions, disturbance, seed sources and alternative paths; avoid fixed year counts.
这是保留土壤条件下的一条次生演替示意路径；进度条没有真实时间单位，不用于预测恢复: One illustrative secondary-succession path with soil retained. Progress has no real time unit and cannot predict recovery dates.
叶片在适宜季节展开；不少树种通过季节性落叶度过不利时期。: Leaves expand in suitable seasons; many species shed them to withstand unfavorable periods.
从树冠的轮廓、枝条与叶片开始，辨认一片森林的外貌。: Start with crown outlines, branches and leaves to recognize a forest's form.
乔木高大，常可见板根、藤本或附生植物；并非每一棵树都具有全部特征。: Tall trees may have buttress roots, vines or epiphytes. No tree necessarily has all these features.
密集的树冠与丰富的林下植物，共同利用立体空间。: Dense crowns and understory plants share three-dimensional space.
针状叶和常见的尖塔形树冠是识别线索；针叶树并不全都常绿，例如落叶松。: Narrow leaves and often pointed crowns are clues. Not all conifers are evergreen; larches shed their needles.
观察较窄的叶片与树冠形状，比较阔叶林的轮廓。: Compare narrow leaves and crown shapes with broadleaf forest.
草本构成连续的背景，乔木散布其间；季节性水分变化、火和食草动物都可能影响结构。: Grasses form a continuous background with scattered trees. Seasonal water, fire and herbivores influence structure.
这里演示的是稀树草原，不把少量乔木当作所有草原的特征。: This is a savanna example; scattered trees are not a feature of every grassland.
节水、储水、深根或广布浅根等策略各有适用条件，不能用单一形态概括所有荒漠植物。: Water conservation, storage and different root systems suit different conditions; one form cannot represent every desert plant.
看起来空旷的地方，也有适应干旱的生命。: Apparently empty places also support drought-adapted life.
长期或季节性水湿条件有利于特殊适应的植物；湿地也可以由灌木或乔木占优势。: Persistent or seasonal wetness favors specialized plants. Shrubs or trees can also dominate wetlands.
沿着水陆交错的边缘，寻找芦苇状挺水植物与浮叶植物。: Look for reed-like emergent plants and floating leaves along the water's edge.
乔木构成上层轮廓，林下还有灌木、草本与幼苗。森林不是许多相同的树简单相加。: Trees define the upper outline, with shrubs, herbs and seedlings below. A forest is more than copies of one tree.
下一章可以逐层打开这片森林。: The next chapter opens these layers.
低矮草本形成连续的绿色背景。仔细看，不同高度、叶形和花色也构成了草地内部的差异。: Low herbs form continuous cover. Differences in height, leaf shape and flower color also vary within grassland.
草地不等于“没有长成的森林”。: Grassland is not simply an unfinished forest.
图中挺水和浮叶植物占据水陆交错带。它们展示了植物对水湿生境的不同适应。: Emergent and floating-leaved plants illustrate different adaptations at the water's edge.
湿地植被并不只有芦苇和水草。: Wetlands contain more than reeds and aquatic herbs.
根系把地上植被与地下环境连接起来。打开根系透视，观察不同方向的分枝与空间分布。: Roots connect vegetation to its underground environment. Reveal branching directions and spatial patterns.
根系形状与比例经过简化，不代表具体树种。: Root shapes and proportions are simplified and not species-specific.
较高的树冠构成森林上层。降低它的不透明度，就能看到原本被遮挡的灌木与草本。: Tall crowns form the upper forest. Reduce their opacity to reveal shrubs and herbs.
树冠层并不意味着只有一种树高。: A canopy does not imply one uniform tree height.
较低矮的木本植物占据林下空间。不同耐阴能力与生长形态帮助植物利用不同的环境。: Short woody plants occupy the understory. Shade tolerance and growth forms allow different uses of the environment.
注意区分灌木与乔木的幼苗。: Distinguish shrubs from young tree seedlings.
草本、蕨类和幼苗出现在林地表层。用“只看草本”去掉遮挡，观察它们的分布。: Herbs, ferns and seedlings occupy the forest floor. Choose Herbs only to inspect their distribution.
从个体走向整体：森林、草原、荒漠等不同植物群落共同构成一个地区的植被。: From individuals to communities: forests, grasslands, deserts and other communities form regional vegetation.
降低乔木层的不透明度后，为什么还能看见其他绿色植物？: Why are green plants still visible when tree opacity is reduced?
森林中存在灌木、草本等不同层次: Forests also contain shrub and herb layers
这些植物都是树上落下的叶子: They are all leaves fallen from trees
所有植物最后都会变成高大乔木: Every plant eventually becomes a tall tree
森林的垂直结构与不同植物的生活型、生长高度和对光照等条件的适应有关。: Vertical structure relates to growth form, height and adaptation to light and other conditions.
关于荒漠植被，哪种说法更准确？: Which statement about desert vegetation is more accurate?
不同植物具有不同的耐旱策略: Different plants use different drought strategies
深根、浅而广的根、减小叶面积、储水和短生等都是可能的适应策略，不能一概而论。: Deep roots, broad shallow roots, reduced leaves, storage and short growth cycles are possible strategies, not universal rules.
这座示意山的林线，能当作所有山地通用的林线吗？: Is this model's treeline universal for all mountains?
可以，树木都在固定海拔停止生长: Yes, trees stop at a fixed elevation
不可以，林线及植被带因地区与环境而异: No, treelines and belts depend on region and conditions
纬度、坡向、山体条件及干扰等都会影响植被带。滑杆表示模型内相对观察高度，不是统一: Latitude, aspect, terrain and disturbance affect belts. The slider shows relative model height, not universal elevation.
同一片温带落叶阔叶林，冬季树冠稀疏主要说明什么？: What does a sparse winter canopy in the same deciduous forest mainly indicate?
树木出现季节性落叶，枝干仍然存在: Seasonal leaf shedding, with branches remaining
季相描述植被外貌随季节的变化。季节性落叶不等于树木死亡，也不等于群落发生演替。: Seasonal appearance changes within a year. Leaf fall is neither tree death nor community succession.
为什么本章称为“次生演替”的示意？: Why is this an example of secondary succession?
起点仍保留土壤，不是从完全没有土壤的基质开始: Soil remains at the start, unlike a soil-free substrate
因为一定会在固定年数内完成: It must finish within a fixed number of years
本章假设干扰后土壤仍在。恢复的路径和时间取决于环境与干扰，不保证最终成为森林。: Soil is assumed to remain after disturbance. Recovery depends on conditions and disturbance and need not end in forest.
亮色观察线标出当前高度的坡面位置。向上移动时，比较植被的高度、密度与生活型。: The bright line marks the current height. Move upward and compare plant height, density and growth forms.
始终观察同一片森林，排除地点差异。拖动季节轴，留意树冠颜色、疏密和枝干显露的变化: Stay in the same forest to remove location differences. Scrub the season axis and compare color, density and exposed branches.
起点保留土壤。植物在同一片地表逐渐定居，群落的优势种类和空间结构随过程改变。: Soil remains initially. Plants colonize the same surface as dominant forms and spatial structure change.
